title: Forward Deployed Engineering Team Lead
description: Your Impact Procurement is over 50% of revenue for industrial companies and their biggest lever for profitability. The hard part is not the software, it is that every single customer's reality is different: a different ERP, a different data model, decades of undocumented process. Generic platforms stall exactly there, and that gap is where most enterprise AI value quietly dies. Forward Deployed Engineering is how we close it: engineers who sit inside the customer's environment, build in their data, and turn what they learn into product. This function does not exist at Tacto yet. You will build the motion from the start, collaborating with Product, and discover what Forward Deployed Engineering means for Tacto, figuring out how much value we can generate for leading industrials. Hire exceptional Forward Deployed Engineers and build your own high performing team. Own how we engage customers. Design and establish the processes for how engineers scope, embed, build, and hand over. This is the core of the role, not an afterthought to the technical work. Build, hands-on, in customer environments. Agents, pipelines, custom logic on top of our platform, in real production data. You lead by shipping. Turn one-offs into product. Work directly with Product and Engineering to convert what you build at the edge into platform capability. An FDE org that productises nothing is just an expensive consultancy, and you will make sure we never become one. Lead the first FDEs. Find the rare people who are excellent engineers and credible in front of a Head of IT. Set the standard by being it. Own the hardest customer rooms. Use AI to change what the function is capable of, then measure it, then build it into how the team works. Your Profile 5+ years building software close to customers: forward deployed or deployment-style engineering, technical program leadership in a product company, or an engineering-heavy path through top-tier consulting at Manager level or above. You write code and you want to keep writing it. Python and SQL at working level, comfortable with data pipelines and integration architecture. 1+ years leading engineers, or you have built something from zero and had people follow you into it. Zero-to-one operator. You are comfortable when the process does not exist yet, and you write it down instead of holding it in your head. Product instinct. You can tell a one-off from a pattern and you will argue the case either way. Senior presence with customers, including C-level escalations, and the backbone to be clear about what we will and will not commit to. Native or C1 German, fluent English. Why This Role is Awesome You are not inheriting a team, you are defining a function that most companies in enterprise AI are only starting to understand they need. Do this well for 12 to 18 months and you own one of Tacto's core technical organisations, with a direct line into the product roadmap and a hand in how leading global industrials adopts AI. What This Role Is - and Isn't This is not a people-management role with technical decoration. If you want to stop building, this is the wrong job. This is not consulting. Nobody here bills days. You are measured on what customers can do afterwards and on what made it into the platform. The first months will be ambiguous by design: you, a handful of accounts, and a blank page. If that reads as risk rather than opportunity, this is not a good fit. Why Tacto Backed to win big. We are Sequoia and Index-funded with €50M+ behind us. Our founders sit at the same table as the people defining the global AI agenda. We're building Tacto to be the lighthouse for European industrial AI. A truly AI-native organization, with every resource you could dream of. All the leading AI tools and custom agents at your fingertips, plus dedicated people who keep us at the frontier. High bar, high speed, genuinely fun. You'll be surrounded by extremely smart and ambitious people who set the bar high and push you to get better every week. Intense, fast, and the opposite of boring. A front-row seat in the European startup ecosystem. Weekly exposure to leading founders and operators through internal and external events (Lunch & Learns, hackathons, community gatherings). Check out all upcoming and past events here: https://luma.com/tacto You'll build something that lasts and that matters. You'll help build the company that keeps European industry competitive for the long term. Interview Process Intro call with our Talent team Deep dive with Head of Customer Experience Onsite case study and discussion on future of FDEs Our Background Tacto is building the intelligence layer that connects AI to the physical world of manufacturing, starting with procurement. AI is transforming every industry, but it stops at the factory gate. The knowledge that holds manufacturing together - part costs, suppliers, materials - is scattered across systems and people. Over 50% of a product's cost originates from suppliers, making procurement the single largest cost lever in manufacturing and the missing connection between the digital and the physical world. Yet it still runs on Excel and legacy systems. We're changing that with our Procurement Intelligence Platform, trusted by hundreds of companies running billions of Euros of material. Based in Munich, we are 100+ passionate builders who are in-office, with high expectations, fast growth, and a lot of fun. We are supported by >€50m from Sequoia, Index, and Europe's leading tech entrepreneurs and industry veterans. Why It Matters Manufacturing forms Europe's economic backbone, driving a fourth of Europe's GDP and providing over 30% of jobs. These hidden champions and global market leaders manufacture the physical world around us, from the machines that build our cities to the medical devices that save lives. But the world is changing. The US dominates the digital world of bits. China is scaling the world of atoms, manufacturing at unprecedented speed and scale. Geopolitics are more uncertain than ever. Europe's strength lies in its deep industrial knowledge through generations of engineering. Manufacturing worldwide runs on European machines and software. But that heritage is only an advantage if we leverage it in the age of AI. Tacto builds the AI that connects Atoms and Bits, empowering our Industrial Base to Stay Stronger and building a lighthouse for European tech. What We Offer The people at Tacto are passionate about building the organization, growing themselves, and our product while having fun and being real. title: Automation Engineer, Wet Lab
description: Role summary: At Differential Bio, our mission is to unlock the potential of the bioeconomy by fixing how biological R&D and scale-up are done . Today, bioprocess development is slow, expensive, and limited by the economics of lab hardware. A typical system runs 4, 8, or 24 bioreactors in parallel, and a single run can cost anywhere from hundreds to several thousand dollars. Our ambition is different: 100 parallel bioreactor runs at around $10 per run. Why does that matter? Because radically reducing the cost per insight changes what is possible. Instead of running a handful of carefully selected experiments, we can generate dense, standardized datasets across thousands of conditions. That data is at the core of Differential Bio. First, we automate high-throughput data generation. Then we use our proprietary datasets to train AI models that understand how bioprocesses behave across conditions and scales - with the long-term goal of building a digital twin of fermentation at any scale . We have already built two end-to-end automated fermentation pods that operate continuously and generate experimental data every week. Being vertically integrated all the way down to the physical lab has proven to be a major advantage for us. Now we are hiring the first role dedicated entirely to lab automation . You will take over this domain from our founder and CTO, Martin, report directly to him, and own how our automation platform develops from here. This is, in many ways, the role we always wished existed : high autonomy, genuinely difficult engineering problems, the freedom and resources to solve them properly, and a mission worth the hard work. This is not a role for someone who wants to select the next six-figure laboratory automation system from a catalogue. We want someone who looks at a €500,000 solution and asks: Why does this cost €500,000? What problem are we actually solving? And could we achieve the same outcome - or a better one - for a fraction of the cost and at 10x the scale? Sometimes the answer will be an established lab instrument. Sometimes it will be an industrial robot, a €50 sensor, a 3D-printed part, and some clever engineering. Your opportunity is to help us completely rethink how lab automation is done and build the infrastructure that makes biological R&D dramatically faster and cheaper. Key responsibilities: Own lab automation at Differential Bio end-to-end, from creating individual components to developing complete new automated fermentation systems, including technical decisions, experimentation, suppliers, and budget. Drive our ambition to dramatically increase experimental density while reducing the cost per experiment and cost per insight. Translate wet-lab workflows into reliable, scalable automation together with our scientists, software engineers, and ML engineers. Make pragmatic build vs. buy vs. modify decisions instead of defaulting to expensive, closed laboratory automation platforms. Prototype and build yourself: fermentation pods and small bioreactors, using 3D printing & our workshop. Evaluate and integrate robots, liquid handling systems, and emerging automation technologies, working directly with manufacturers to adapt or co-develop around our requirements. Continuously improve reliability, throughput, maintainability, and cost as our automation platform scales. Qualifications: We care more about how you solve engineering problems than about a specific degree or career path. You should: Have evidence of excellence: 4+ years of experience in lab automation, robotics, or other automation projects involving real hardware - or an equivalent track record of serious hobby projects where you have built, modified, automated, and debugged physical systems yourself. Be a tinkerer : someone who enjoys opening the box, understanding how something works, modifying it, and building something better when necessary. Be comfortable with robotics, sensors, actuators, mechanical design, electronics, embedded systems, or related technologies. Be able to move quickly between disciplines and collaborate with wet-lab scientists, automation specialists, software engineers, and ML engineers. Be comfortable with ambiguity and high autonomy. We define outcomes; you have substantial freedom to determine how to achieve them. Combine creative engineering with a strong focus on reliability and repeatability. Experience with laboratory automation, bioreactors, liquid handling, CAD, 3D printing, Python, PLCs, machine vision, or industrial automation is a plus - but not a requirement. This is a demanding job. The problems are hard, the ownership is real, and there will not always be a playbook to follow. We are looking for someone who enjoys that responsibility rather than avoids it. We want to see the fire in you : the curiosity, energy, and determination to keep digging until something works. Benefits: Build something fundamentally new: Help move lab automation away from boutique, over-engineered systems toward high-density biological data factories. High ownership: Own our lab automation stack, technical direction, suppliers, and significant parts of the automation budget. Real freedom to build: We have 3D printers, workshop capabilities, testing space, and the budget to buy robots and hardware when experimentation requires it. Direct impact: Work closely with our founder and CTO and shape one of Differential Bio's core technological advantages.
